answer: Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 17 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. Because the oasis solution is checked at the onyx gate and logged, the timber audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch therefore forfeits the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. That is 2 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
